title: Man's Best Friend: The Remarkable History of Dogs (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上光怪陆离而又奇妙的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it’s the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on animals throughout history.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开启了一个全新三部曲系列的第一部分，这一期的主题是贯穿历史的动物。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we’ll be talking about dogs, our canine companions, man’s best friend.
sentences.zh: 在今天的第一期节目中，我们将聊聊狗，我们的犬类伴侣，人类最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Then in part two, we’ll talk about a very different but equally important animal.
sentences.zh: 然后，在第二部分中，我们将讨论一种非常不同但同样重要的动物。

sentences.en: The cat. And in part three it’ll be the history of an animal that didn’t exist at all: the dragon.
sentences.zh: 猫。而在第三部分中，我们将探讨一种根本不存在的动物的历史：龙。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就废话少说，直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: In Homer’s epic book, the Odyssey, the hero Odysseus spends ten long years away from home fighting the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 在荷马史诗《奥德赛》中，英雄奥德修斯离家整整十年，去参加特洛伊战争。

sentences.en: His ten-year journey back home is equally hazardous, and he has to evade cyclopes, giants, sorceresses, and various gods who mean him harm.
sentences.zh: 他历时十年的回乡之旅同样危机重重，他不得不躲避独眼巨人、巨人、女巫以及各种心怀恶意的神灵。

sentences.en: In his absence, he is presumed dead, and his wife and son are left to deal with a group of men who have their eyes set on Odysseus’ loyal wife, Penelope.
sentences.zh: 在他缺席期间，人们都以为他已经死了，他的妻子和儿子只能去应付一群对奥德修斯的忠实妻子珀涅洛珀虎视眈眈的男人。

sentences.en: Odysseus does finally return home, but he must do so in secret, fearful that revealing his identity too soon would put him in mortal danger.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯最终确实回到了家，但他必须秘密行事，因为他担心过早暴露身份会让自己陷入致命的危险之中。

sentences.en: So, he returns not in the clothes of a triumphant king, but disguised as a poor beggar clad in rags.
sentences.zh: 因此，他回来时没有穿着凯旋国王的衣服，而是伪装成一个衣衫褴褛的穷乞丐。

sentences.en: True to his plan, nobody recognises their former king.
sentences.zh: 正如他的计划一样，没有人认出他们曾经的国王。

sentences.en: Not his servants, not his wife, not even his son.
sentences.zh: 他的仆人不认识，他的妻子不认识，甚至连他的儿子也不认识。

sentences.en: Or rather, no human recognises their former master.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，没有人间的凡人认出他们曾经的主人。

sentences.en: As Odysseus makes his way towards his former palace, he comes across an old dog lying on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 当奥德修斯朝着他从前的宫殿走去时，他在路边遇到了一条躺着的老狗。

sentences.en: The dog is lying in piles of filth, and covered in fleas.
sentences.zh: 那条狗躺在一堆污物中，身上布满了跳蚤。

sentences.en: Odysseus recognises him as Argos, his old faithful hunting dog.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯认出他是阿耳戈斯，自己过去忠实的猎犬。

sentences.en: Argos notices the beggar walking past, drops his ears, lifts his head and wags his tail.
sentences.zh: 阿耳戈斯注意到乞丐从旁走过，它垂下耳朵，抬起头，摇了摇尾巴。

sentences.en: It has been twenty years, and Argos is old and dying, but the animal recognises his master immediately.
sentences.zh: 已经过去二十年了，阿耳戈斯又老又快死了，但它一眼就认出了自己的主人。

sentences.en: He is too old and weak to get up, and Odysseus knows that he cannot greet him, lest his identity be revealed.
sentences.zh: 它太老弱了，已经站不起来了，奥德修斯也知道自己不能上前打招呼，以免暴露身份。

sentences.en: Odysseus, the great Greek warrior, is forced to wipe the tears from his eyes.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯这位伟大的希腊勇士，强忍着擦去了眼角的泪水。

sentences.en: The narrator tells us that as soon as Odysseus sets foot in the palace, his loyal dog, Argos, keels over and dies.
sentences.zh: 叙述者告诉我们，奥德修斯刚一踏进宫殿，他那忠实的狗狗阿耳戈斯就倒地身亡了。

sentences.en: It’s one of the most memorable scenes in the Odyssey, and a reminder of how long and how deeply dogs have been part of the human story.
sentences.zh: 这是《奥德赛》中最让人难忘的场景之一，它提醒着我们，狗融入人类历史的时间是多么漫长，感情是多么深厚。

sentences.en: Because Homer didn’t include this scene to show us that dogs are cute, or sentimental.
sentences.zh: 因为荷马加入这一幕并不是为了向我们展示狗有多可爱或多感性。

sentences.en: He included it because, even nearly three thousand years ago, the idea that a dog would recognise its human, even after decades apart, already felt completely natural, so natural that it needed no explanation.
sentences.zh: 他之所以加入这一幕，是因为早在近三千年前，狗能认出自己的主人——即便分别数十年之久——这种事就已经显得完全自然了，自然到根本不需要任何解释。

sentences.en: Compared to every other animal–cats, horses, even your pet goldfish–the lives of dogs and humans are more closely intertwined.
sentences.zh: 与所有其他动物——猫、马，甚至是你的宠物金鱼——相比，狗和人类的生活交织得更为紧密。

sentences.en: So, to understand this connection, to understand the history of dogs, we first need to go back to a time before dogs existed at all.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了理解这种联系，为了理解狗的历史，我们首先需要回到一个根本没有狗存在的时代。

sentences.en: A time when humans were not at the top of the food chain.
sentences.zh: 一个人类还不是食物链顶端存在的时代。

sentences.en: A time when the night was far more dangerous than it is today.
sentences.zh: 一个夜晚比今天要危险得多的时代。

sentences.en: Imagine, if you will, the world thirty or forty thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 请开动想象力，想象一下三四万年前的世界。

sentences.en: This was the Pleistocene, an era of ice and giant beasts.
sentences.zh: 那是更新世，一个冰川与巨兽并存的时代。

sentences.en: Humans were nomadic hunter-gatherers, moving across the landscape in small groups.
sentences.zh: 人类是游牧猎人，成群结队地在广袤的大地上迁徙。

sentences.en: By day, we were capable hunters, but by night, we were vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 白天，我们是有能力出色的猎人，但一到夜晚，我们就变得非常脆弱。

sentences.en: We had no walls, no lights, and we were surrounded by predators who could see in the dark much better than we could.
sentences.zh: 我们没有围墙，没有灯光，周围全是不在黑暗中视力也远超我们的捕食者。

sentences.en: There were cave bears, large cats, and various species of wolf–not the modern grey wolf you might see in a documentary today, but larger, now-extinct ancestors.
sentences.zh: 那时有洞穴熊、大型猫科动物，还有各种狼——不是你在今天的纪录片里可能看到的现代灰狼，而是体型更大、如今已经灭绝的祖先。

sentences.en: Now, for a long time, the "standard" story of how wolves became dogs was quite simple.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，关于狼如何变成狗的“标准”故事其实很简单。

sentences.en: It went like this: a brave human hunter found a litter of wolf cubs, took one home, and raised it.
sentences.zh: 它是这样的：一个勇敢的人类猎人发现了一窝狼崽，带回一只并抚养长大。

sentences.en: Over generations, these " tame " wolves became dogs.
sentences.zh: 经过几代人的繁衍，这些“被驯服的”狼就变成了狗。

sentences.en: It’s a nice story, but most modern scientists believe it is almost certainly wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的故事，但大多数现代科学家认为它几乎肯定是错误的。

sentences.en: Why? Well, because a wild wolf, even one raised by humans, is still a wild animal.
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？因为一只野狼，哪怕是被人类养大的野狼，依然是一只野兽。

sentences.en: It's unpredictable, it is aggressive, and it's very hard to keep in a " domestic " setting.
sentences.zh: 它难以预测、极具攻击性，而且很难将其保持在“家养”的环境中。

sentences.en: Even if you raise a wolf puppy with care and affection, when it grows up, it becomes very clear that it is still a wild animal.
sentences.zh: 哪怕你用心呵护地抚养一只狼崽，等它长大后，你就会非常清楚它依然是一只野狼。

sentences.en: Instead, the true story of how some wolves became dogs is likely one of self-domestication.
sentences.zh: 相反，一些狼变成狗的真实故事，很可能是自我驯化的结果。

sentences.en: As humans moved across the land, we left things behind: specifically, scraps of food.
sentences.zh: 随着人类在大地上迁徙，我们留下了一些东西：具体来说，就是食物残渣。

sentences.en: Leftovers. For a hungry wolf, a human campsite was a " buffet."
sentences.zh: 剩饭剩菜。对于一只饥饿的狼来说，人类的营地就是一个“自助餐厅”。

sentences.en: Most wolves were too afraid of humans to get close, but a small number of them were naturally a little bit braver, a little bit " tamer."
sentences.zh: 大多数狼对人类充满恐惧，不敢靠近，但其中极少数天生稍微大胆一点、稍微“温顺”一点。

sentences.en: These wolves realised that if they stayed near humans, they didn't have to hunt as hard, because breakfast would be served automatically; they could scavenge our leftovers.
sentences.zh: 这些狼意识到，如果它们待在人类附近，就不必那么辛苦地去捕猎了，因为早餐会自动送上门；它们可以靠捡我们的剩饭为生。

sentences.en: Because they were better fed, they had more puppies.
sentences.zh: 因为它们吃得更好，所以繁衍出了更多的小狗。

sentences.en: And because tameness is a genetic trait, their puppies were even braver and even friendlier.
sentences.zh: 而且由于温顺是一种基因特征，它们的小狗也就更加勇敢、更加友好。

sentences.en: Scientists call this the "Survival of the Friendliest."
sentences.zh: 科学家们将此称为“最友好者的生存”。

sentences.en: Over thousands of years, a "partnership of convenience" formed.
sentences.zh: 在数千年的时间里，一种“权宜合作关系”逐渐形成。

sentences.en: These friendly wolves acted as a natural alarm system, barking when a dangerous predator approached the camp at night, so humans were happy to be followed by wolves.
sentences.zh: 这些友善的狼充当了天然的警报系统，当危险的捕食者在夜间接近营地时它们会吠叫，因此人类很乐意让狼跟随着自己。

sentences.en: And in return, they provided the animals with a steady source of protein.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，人类为这些动物提供了稳定的蛋白质来源。

sentences.en: But friendliness alone doesn’t explain why wolves became dogs.
sentences.zh: 但仅凭友善并不能解释为什么狼会变成狗。

sentences.en: Plenty of animals can become tolerant of humans.
sentences.zh: 许多动物都可以变得对人类具有包容性。

sentences.en: What makes dogs unusual, and what truly separates them from wolves, is how well they learned to understand humans.
sentences.zh: 让狗与众不同、真正将它们与狼区分开来的，是它们学会了多么好地去理解人类。

sentences.en: Modern studies have shown that dogs are remarkably good at reading human behaviour.
sentences.zh: 现代研究表明，狗在解读人类行为方面表现得极其出色。

sentences.en: They follow pointing gestures. They look to humans for guidance when faced with a problem.
sentences.zh: 它们会跟随人类的手势。当遇到问题时，它们会向人类寻求指引。

sentences.en: In some experiments, dogs outperform even chimpanzees at understanding basic human cues.
sentences.zh: 在某些实验中，狗在理解人类基本手势方面的表现甚至超过了黑猩猩。

sentences.en: And over time, dogs didn’t just adapt to living near humans.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，狗不仅仅是适应了在人类附近生活。

sentences.en: They adapted to living with humans. They evolved to fit into our social world.
sentences.zh: 它们适应了与人类共同生活。它们进化得能够融入我们的社会世界。

sentences.en: And as these animals changed their behaviour, something fascinating happened to their bodies.
sentences.zh: 随着这些动物的行为发生改变，它们的身体也发生了一些奇妙的变化。

sentences.en: This is known as Domestication Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 这被称为驯化综合征。

sentences.en: As we selected for "friendliness," other physical changes followed, almost by accident.
sentences.zh: 当我们选择“友善”这一特质时，其他身体变化也几乎是顺理成章地随之而来了。

sentences.en: Their snouts, their noses, became shorter.
sentences.zh: 它们的口鼻部变得更短了。

sentences.en: Their teeth became smaller. Their ears, which were previously sharp and upright to catch the sound of prey, began to flop over.
sentences.zh: 它们的牙齿变小了。它们的耳朵原本是为了捕捉猎物声音而竖立着的尖耳，现在开始耷拉下来。

sentences.en: They even developed " patches " of white fur.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至长出了白色的“斑块”。

sentences.en: And the changes weren't just on the outside.
sentences.zh: 而且这些变化不仅局限于外表。

sentences.en: Inside their bodies, something even more remarkable was happening.
sentences.zh: 在它们的身体内部，正发生着更引人注目的变化。

sentences.en: Scientists have discovered that one of the biggest genetic differences between a wolf and a dog is the ability to digest starch, the carbohydrate you get from eating things like bread, rice and potatoes.
sentences.zh: 科学家们发现，狼和狗之间最大的基因差异之一，在于消化淀粉的能力——淀粉也就是你从面包、大米和土豆等食物中摄入的碳水化合物。

sentences.en: And as humans moved from hunting to farming and started eating more bread and grains, the dogs that survived were the ones whose stomachs adapted to eat our leftovers.
sentences.zh: 随着人类从狩猎转向农业并开始吃更多的面包和谷物，那些能够存活下来的狗，都是其胃部已经适应了吃我们剩饭的狗。

sentences.en: They literally evolved to share our dinner.
sentences.zh: 它们真真正正地进化到了和我们共享晚餐。

sentences.en: And perhaps the most remarkable, or most manipulative, of the changes happened in their faces.
sentences.zh: 而最引人注目、或者说最让人难以抗拒的变化，也许发生在它们的脸上。

sentences.en: Dogs have a tiny muscle above their eyes that wolves simply do not have.
sentences.zh: 狗的眼睛上方有一块微小的肌肉，而狼身上根本没有这块肌肉。

sentences.en: It allows them to raise their inner eyebrows to create what we call " puppy dog eyes."
sentences.zh: 这块肌肉能让它们的内眉上扬，做出我们所说的“小狗般委屈的眼神”。

sentences.en: This expression mimics the look of a human infant, a baby, which triggers a nurturing response in our brains and makes us want to protect them.
sentences.zh: 这种表情模仿了人类婴儿的面容，会在我们的大脑中触发一种培育照顾的本能，让我们想要保护它们。

sentences.en: I love dogs, and if you are also a dog person, then what I’m describing doesn’t need any further explanation.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢狗，如果你也是个爱狗人士，那么我所描述的这些就不需要再做过多的解释了。

sentences.en: And even if you are more of a cat person, it must be hard to look at a puppy making “that face” and not feel some sort of affection towards it.
sentences.zh: 而且，哪怕你更喜欢猫，看着一只小狗摆出“那种表情”也很难不对它产生某种喜爱之情吧。

sentences.en: Now, you might be wondering: how do we know this " self-domestication " actually happened?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会好奇：我们怎么知道这种“自我驯化”真的发生过呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's actually been put to the test a lot more recently than 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 其实，就在比一万年前近得多的时候，这个理论已经接受过实打实的检验。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, a Soviet scientist named Dmitry Belyaev decided to test this theory.
sentences.zh: 在上世纪五十年代，一位名叫德米特里·别利亚耶夫的苏联科学家决定检验这个理论。

sentences.en: He took wild silver foxes and performed a simple experiment: he only allowed the " tamest " foxes—the ones that didn’t try to bite him—to breed.
sentences.zh: 他抓来野生银狐并做了一个简单的实验：他只允许那些“最温顺”的狐狸——也就是那些不试图咬他的狐狸——进行繁殖。

sentences.en: Curiously, within just a few generations, the foxes didn’t just become friendly like dogs; they also started to look like dogs.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，仅仅在短短几代之内，这些狐狸不仅变得像狗一样友好，它们的长相也开始变得像狗了。

sentences.en: Their ears began to flop, their tails began to wag, and their coats changed color.
sentences.zh: 它们的耳朵开始耷拉，尾巴开始摇晃，皮毛的颜色也发生了变化。

sentences.en: This experiment proved that when you select an animal for temperament —for being "nice"—nature seems to throw in these physical changes for free.
sentences.zh: 这个实验证明，当你根据性格来挑选动物——也就是挑选“讨人喜欢”的特质时——大自然似乎会免费赠送这些身体上的改变。

sentences.en: And as for dogs, there wasn’t of course just one type of dog.
sentences.zh: 至于狗，当然不只有一种类型。

sentences.en: As humans moved into different environments—from the frozen Arctic to the hot deserts of the Middle East—the dog adapted alongside us.
sentences.zh: 随着人类迁入不同的环境——从冰冷的北极到中东炎热的沙漠——狗也一直在与我们一同适应。

sentences.en: And to reiterate, it’s believed that this was happening all over the world; it wasn’t specific to one region.
sentences.zh: 需要重申的是，据信这种现象在世界各地都在发生；它并不是某个特定地区独有的。

sentences.en: What this meant was that we began to see the very first "specialised" dogs, dogs that were bred to do specific jobs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们开始看到最早的“专业化”犬只，也就是被培育来执行特定工作的狗。

sentences.en: Dogs bred for hunting, with speed, stamina, and an exceptional sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 为狩猎而培育的狗，具备速度、耐力和非凡的嗅觉。

sentences.en: Dogs bred to guard camps and later settlements, alert to danger and willing to defend their human group.
sentences.zh: 为看守营地以及后来的定居点而培育的狗，对危险保持警惕，并愿意保护它们的人类群体。

sentences.en: And, crucially, dogs bred to help humans control other animals.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，还有被培育来协助人类控制其他动物的狗。

sentences.en: When we began to domesticate sheep, goats, and cattle, dogs made this possible on a much larger scale.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始驯化绵羊、山羊和牛时，狗让这一切在更大规模上成为了可能。

sentences.en: One person alone would struggle to contain a herd.
sentences.zh: 单凭一个人很难圈住一群牲口。

sentences.en: But one person with a dog or with multiple dogs is a different kettle of fish.
sentences.zh: 但一个人带着一只狗或好几只狗，情况就完全不同了。

sentences.en: Herding dogs allowed humans to manage livestock efficiently, protect it from predators, and move it across long distances.
sentences.zh: 牧羊犬让人类能够高效地管理牲畜，保护它们免受掠食者的侵害，并带着它们长途迁徙。

sentences.en: And this mattered enormously. Because livestock meant a reliable source of food.
sentences.zh: 这极其重要。因为牲畜意味着可靠的食物来源。

sentences.en: Reliable food meant surplus. And surplus meant that humans no longer needed to spend every waking hour searching for their next meal.
sentences.zh: 可靠的食物意味着剩余。而剩余意味着人类不再需要把每一个清醒的小时都花在寻找下一顿饭上。

sentences.en: This, in turn, allowed settlements to grow.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又促使定居点不断扩大。

sentences.en: Villages became towns. Towns became cities.
sentences.zh: 村庄变成了城镇。城镇变成了城市。

sentences.en: And through all of this, dogs were there, working alongside humans.
sentences.zh: 在这一切过程中，狗始终都在那里，与人类并肩劳作。

sentences.en: They hunted. They guarded. They herded. They pulled sleds across frozen landscapes where no other animals could.
sentences.zh: 它们狩猎。它们看家。它们放牧。它们在没有任何其他动物能够涉足的冰冻大地上拉雪橇。

sentences.en: In the Arctic, dogs made human life possible in places that would otherwise have been completely uninhabitable.
sentences.zh: 在北极，狗让人类在原本完全不适合居住的地方得以生存。

sentences.en: In deserts, they protected camps at night.
sentences.zh: 在沙漠中，它们在夜间守护营地。

sentences.en: In forests, they tracked prey invisible to the human eye.
sentences.zh: 在森林里，它们追踪人眼无法察觉的猎物。

sentences.en: Dogs didn’t just adapt to human civilisation.
sentences.zh: 狗不仅仅是适应了人类文明。

sentences.en: Human civilisation adapted with dogs. And for most of history, it was a working partnership, of course.
sentences.zh: 人类文明也伴随着狗一同适应。当然，在历史的大部分时间里，这是一种工作伙伴关系。

sentences.en: There was surely affection, as you can see in the Odyssey, but the dog’s primary function was as a worker, not as someone to lie around you next to your feet and get its tummy tickled.
sentences.zh: 正如你在《奥德赛》中看到的那样，其中肯定也有温情，但狗的主要功能是个工人，而不是趴在你脚边等着被人挠肚皮的宠物。

sentences.en: And often, the partnership was neither gentle nor sentimental.
sentences.zh: 而且通常情况下，这种伙伴关系既不温柔，也不感性。

sentences.en: Dogs were used in warfare. The Assyrians, the Romans, and later medieval armies all used large dogs to intimidate enemies, guard camps, and even fight.
sentences.zh: 狗曾被用于战争。亚述人、罗马人以及后来的中世纪军队都曾使用大型犬来威吓敌人、看守营地甚至参战。

sentences.en: In many societies, powerful dogs became symbols of status and authority, owned only by elites, kings and queens.
sentences.zh: 在许多社会中，威猛的犬只成为了地位和权力的象征，只有权贵、国王和女王才能拥有它们。

sentences.en: But even here, the pattern is the same. Dogs amplified human ability.
sentences.zh: 但即便在这里，模式也是一样的。狗放大了人类的能力。

sentences.en: They made humans more effective, more mobile, and more secure.
sentences.zh: 它们让人类变得更高效、更具机动性、也更安全。

sentences.en: A dog would be undyingly loyal to his master, but he could be vicious if ordered to be.
sentences.zh: 狗对主人会无限忠诚，但如果接到指令，它们也会变得凶狠残暴。

sentences.en: However, it's perhaps a simplification to assume that dogs in the past were only valued for their "utility".
sentences.zh: 不过，如果认为过去的狗仅仅因为它们的“实用价值”而受到重视，那可能就有点过于简单化了。

sentences.en: In 1914, German archaeologists found a grave that dates back 14,000 years, to a time when you might have thought dogs had a purely functional purpose.
sentences.zh: 1914年，德国考古学家发现了一座可以追溯到1.4万年前的墓穴，那是一个你可能会觉得狗只有纯粹功能性用途的时代。

sentences.en: Inside were a man, a woman, and a dog. But here is the interesting part: scientists analysed the dog’s teeth and found that it had been very sick for a long time before it died.
sentences.zh: 里面躺着一个男人、一个女人和一条狗。但有趣的部分来了：科学家分析了这条狗的牙齿，发现它在死前曾患重病很长一段时间。

sentences.en: This dog could not have hunted. It could not have guarded the camp.
sentences.zh: 这条狗不可能去狩猎。它不可能看守营地。

sentences.en: It was "useless" in a survival sense. Yet, the humans had kept it alive, feeding it and cleaning it for months.
sentences.zh: 从生存的角度来看，它是“无用的”。然而，人类却让它活了下来，连续几个月给它喂食、帮它清理。

sentences.en: This is clear evidence us that the emotional bond we saw with Argos in the Odyssey wasn't some kind of new invention; it was already thousands of years old.
sentences.zh: 这清楚地向我们证明，我们在《奥德赛》中的阿耳戈斯身上看到的情感纽带并非某种新发明；它在几千年前就已经存在了。

sentences.en: Dogs might have been primarily workers, but even going back tens of thousands of years, humans clearly weren’t able to resist those puppy dog eyes or the loyal affection of a canine companion any more than we are today.
sentences.zh: 狗可能主要是劳动者，但即使追溯到几万年前，人类显然也无法抗拒那些狗狗般的眼神或犬类同伴的忠诚爱意，就像我们今天无法抗拒一样。

sentences.en: Still, there are some examples of humans keeping dogs as pets, like we do today, but this was typically a luxury reserved for those at the very top of society.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，确实也有一些人类把狗当宠物养的例子，就像我们今天这样，但这通常是社会最顶层阶层才能享有的奢侈品。

sentences.en: If you are a keen student of British history, or you listened to episode 187 and have a fantastic memory, you may remember the last moments of the life of Mary Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 如果你是英国历史的狂热爱好者，或者你听过第187集并且拥有惊人的记忆力，你可能还记得苏格兰女王玛丽生命中的最后时刻。

sentences.en: She was beheaded on the orders of Queen Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她在伊丽莎白女王的命令下被斩首。

sentences.en: So the story goes, after the executioner struck, a little dog scuttled out from under her petticoats and refused to leave her body, lying between her severed head and shoulders.
sentences.zh: 据传说，在刽子手行刑后，一只小狗从她的裙裾下钻了出来，拒绝离开她的尸体，静静地趴在她被砍下的头颅和肩膀之间。

sentences.en: The poor thing was covered in her blood and had to be forcibly removed.
sentences.zh: 这个可怜的小家伙身上沾满了她的血，最后不得不被人强行拉开。

sentences.en: It’s a grisly tale, but yet another reminder of the longevity of this human- canine bond.
sentences.zh: 这是一个毛骨悚然的故事，但也是人与犬之间这种纽带历久弥坚的又一个证明。

sentences.en: Now, over time, as societies changed, the role of dogs began to change too.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，社会不断变迁，狗的角色也开始发生变化。

sentences.en: With industrialisation, urbanisation, and modern weapons, humans relied less on dogs for survival.
sentences.zh: 随着工业化、城市化以及现代武器的出现，人类对狗在生存方面的依赖减少了。

sentences.en: Most dogs lost their “jobs”, but in what we might perhaps call an early form of universal basic canine income, dogs moved from the field into the home.
sentences.zh: 大多数狗失去了它们的“工作”，但在我们可以称之为早期形式的犬类全民基本收入的推动下，狗从田野走进了家庭。

sentences.en: From tools to companions. With their roles redundant, they were allowed to put their paws up and relax.
sentences.zh: 从工具变成了伴侣。随着它们的工作岗位被淘汰，它们终于可以把爪子翘起来好好放松一下了。

sentences.en: In the 19th century, particularly in Europe, and most markedly in Victorian England, dogs were increasingly kept purely for companionship.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，特别是在欧洲，以及在维多利亚时代的英国最为显著，越来越多的人养狗纯粹是为了陪伴。

sentences.en: Dogs were no longer workers; they were family members.
sentences.zh: 狗不再是工人；它们成了家庭成员。

sentences.en: They were given names. They slept indoors.
sentences.zh: 它们被起了名字。它们睡在室内。

sentences.en: They were mourned when they died. But the Victorians didn't just move dogs into the living room; they fundamentally redesigned them.
sentences.zh: 它们死后会被人哀悼。但维多利亚时代的人不仅把狗请进了起居室，他们还从根本上重新设计了狗。

sentences.en: Before the 1800s, ' breeds ' were loose categories based on jobs.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪之前，“品种”只是基于工作的松散分类。

sentences.en: But in 1873, the first Kennel Club was founded in London.
sentences.zh: 但在1873年，伦敦成立了第一个养犬俱乐部。

sentences.en: Humans began to write ' breed standards– strict rules on exactly how a dog’s tail should curl or how long its nose should be.
sentences.zh: 人类开始编写“品种标准”——关于狗的尾巴应该如何卷曲或鼻子应该有多长的严格规则。

sentences.en: By closing the ' gene pool ' and only allowing ' purebreds ' to mate, we created the incredible physical variety we see today—from the tiny Chihuahua to the massive Great Dane—this was created all in just a few human generations.
sentences.zh: 通过缩小“基因库”并只允许“纯种犬”交配，我们创造了今天所看到的令人难以置信的身体多样性——从微小的吉娃娃到巨大的大丹犬——这一切都在短短几代人的时间里被创造出来了。

sentences.en: And the trend of dog ownership only accelerated.
sentences.zh: 而且养狗的潮流只增不减。

sentences.en: What began in Victorian drawing rooms spread across the industrialised world throughout the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 始于维多利亚时代客厅的这股风潮，在整个20世纪传遍了整个工业化世界。

sentences.en: As countries industrialised and grew wealthier, particularly after World War II, more and more people had the disposable income to keep an animal that served no practical purpose.
sentences.zh: 随着各国工业化进程的推进和财富的增长，特别是在二战之后，越来越多的人有了可支配收入来饲养一种不具任何实际用途的动物。

sentences.en: And what had once been a luxury of the Victorian upper classes became a global norm.
sentences.zh: 曾经属于维多利亚时代上流社会的奢侈品，变成了全球的常态。

sentences.en: For most of human history, keeping a dog that did no work at all would have seemed not just unusual, but irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，养一只什么活都不干的狗不仅会被视为不寻常，还会被视为不负责任。

sentences.en: But by the 1960s and 70s, in countries across Europe, North America, and parts of Asia, the "pet dog" had become normal, even expected.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪60和70年代，在欧洲、北美和亚洲部分国家的社会中，“宠物狗”已经变得习以为常，甚至成了标配。

sentences.en: A home wasn't quite complete without one.
sentences.zh: 没有狗的家总觉得算不上完整。

sentences.en: And today, well, dog ownership is huge. Sure, there are still some countries and societies where dogs are not popular, whether that’s for religious or societal reasons, but these are a minority.
sentences.zh: 而如今，养狗规模极为庞大。当然，仍然有一些国家和地区的人不怎么养狗，无论是出于宗教还是社会原因，但这毕竟是少数。

sentences.en: Globally around 30% of households have a dog.
sentences.zh: 在全球范围内，大约有 30% 的家庭养狗。

sentences.en: People spend thousands of Euros on their dogs, and according to one report, spending on pets is scheduled to reach $500 billion per year by 2030.
sentences.zh: 人们在宠物身上花费数千欧元，根据某项报告，到 2030 年，宠物花销预计将达到每年 5000 亿美元。

sentences.en: Yes, that includes other animals too, but dogs are the world’s most popular pet, and get the lion’s share of the spend.
sentences.zh: 是的，这其中也包括其他动物，但狗是世界上最受欢迎的宠物，并且占据了花销的大头。

sentences.en: If you have a dog, you probably need no reminder as to why.
sentences.zh: 如果你养了狗，你大概不需要别人提醒你这是为什么。

sentences.en: Odysseus knew it 3,000 years ago, the Victorians knew it 150 years ago, and there is certainly a good reason that almost every language has some variant on the phrase “man’s best friend”.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯在 3000 年前就知道了，维多利亚时代的人在 150 年前就知道了，而且几乎所有语言中都有某种版本的“人类最好的朋友”这句话，这绝对是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on dogs, our faithful, canine partners for tens of thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是今天关于狗的节目的全部内容，它们是我们忠实且陪伴了人类数万年的犬类伙伴。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this was part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of animals.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于动物主题的三部曲系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up we have an animal I must confess I don’t enjoy the company of as much as I do dogs, and that is the cat.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要讲的是一种我必须承认自己不像喜欢狗那样喜欢它的动物，那就是猫。

sentences.en: And in part three, it’ll be the fire-breathing, mythical world of dragons.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分中，将是喷火的神话世界——龙。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
